title: Library
intro: Work on ELIZA, Joseph Weizenbaum and the ELIZA effect, being added to. A work is held here where its licence allows, and otherwise linked to where it is published or cited.

items.title: Mixed-Reality Interfaces and the ELIZA Effect
items.author: Fedorova, Ksenia
items.in: Tactics of Interfacing: Encoding Affect in Art and Technology, The MIT Press
items.note: Chapter, pp. 143-190, applying the ELIZA effect to mixed-reality interfaces in art and technology.

items.title: Scientists Have Resurrected ELIZA, the World's First Chatbot
items.author: Gault, Matthew
items.note: Report that the original code, once thought lost, was found and made to run again.

items.title: Review of Inventing Eliza from The MIT Press
items.note: Unsigned online review describing the book's coverage of the recovered code, Weizenbaum, the cultural context of ELIZA and its link to present chatbots, and recommending it.

items.title: A Study of the Relationship Between Personality Factors, Attitudes, and Measured Content in a Computerized Counseling Interview
items.author: Ralston, H. Robert
items.note: Master's-level study using an adapted Eliza program with 42 high school students to relate personality and attitude measures to the content of a computerised counselling interview.

items.title: Computer power and human reason
items.author: Shotwell, D. A.
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: Joseph Weizenbaum
items.note: Student newspaper obituary saying Weizenbaum grew sceptical of artificial intelligence after a program made users feel they were speaking with an empathic psychologist.

items.title: The Weizenbaum controversy
items.author: Schank, Roger C.
items.note: Schank enters the debate after Weizenbaum's reply to McCarthy's SIGART review, responding to the use of his name and research in it.

items.title: Joseph Weizenbaum. Computer Power and Human Reason: From Judgment to Calculation
items.author: Bierstedt, Robert
items.in: The Annals of the American Academy of Political and Social Science 426(1): 266-267
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: The Autonomous Self in the Age of Automation: Joseph Weizenbaum and the Intellectual History of AI Criticism, c. 1950-1990
items.author: Rust, Magnus
items.publisher: University of Basel, Media Studies (dissertation project)
items.note: Doctoral project page, thesis in progress, on Weizenbaum's life and work from ERMA onward, including the psychiatric contacts in the San Francisco Bay Area that shaped the research design of ELIZA.

items.title: ChatGPT bénéficie-t-il d'une forme d'effet Eliza ?: Une analyse socio-technique
items.author: Marcoccia, Michel; Gauducheau, Nadia; Bénel, Aurélien
items.note: Asks whether current enthusiasm for ChatGPT resembles what Weizenbaum observed in 1966 with the DOCTOR script of ELIZA, using a socio-technical analysis.

items.title: A Computer and Its Man
items.author: Shapiro, Norman Z.
items.note: Comments on Weizenbaum's book by way of ELIZA, asking who the joke was on once the program's creator had written about it.

items.title: Weizenbaum, Creator of ELIZA Program, Dies
items.note: Radio obituary built around ELIZA as a program that users treated as a good listener and around the controversy it caused.

items.title: The ELIZA Effect
items.author: Natale, Simone
items.in: Deceitful Media: Artificial Intelligence and Social Life after the Turing Test, Oxford University Press
items.note: Chapter 3, pp. 50-67, on Weizenbaum's development of ELIZA at MIT and the emergence of chatbots, framed within the book's account of banal deception in AI.

items.title: Joseph Weizenbaum, professor emeritus of computer science, 85
items.note: MIT obituary recording Weizenbaum's death in Berlin and his creation of ELIZA, and his later scepticism about artificial intelligence.

items.title: Three Reviews of J. Weizenbaum's Computer Power and Human Reason
items.author: Buchanan, Bruce G.; Lederberg, Joshua; McCarthy, John
items.publisher: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Memo AIM-291 / STAN-CS-76-577; DTIC ADA044713
items.note: Reprints reviews of the book by Buchanan, Lederberg and McCarthy together with Weizenbaum's reply to McCarthy.

items.title: Eliza Program
items.author: O'Regan, Gerard
items.in: The Innovation in Computing Companion, Springer
items.note: Short reference chapter, pp. 119-122, on the ELIZA program.

items.title: “Machine Down” ::making sense of human–computer interaction—Garfinkel’s research on ELIZA and LYRIC from 1967 to 1969 and its contemporary relevance
items.author: Eisenmann, Clemens; Mlynář, Jakub; Turowetz, Jason J.; Rawls, Anne Warfield
items.note: Examines Harold Garfinkel's work with ELIZA and the related program LYRIC from 1967 to 1969.

items.title: The ELIZA Effect
items.author: Mars, Roman
items.note: Episode with published text telling the story of ELIZA at MIT, the responses of its users, and Weizenbaum's turn against the AI field.

items.title: Założenia polskiego systemu konwersacyjnego MARYSIA
items.author: Bień, Janusz Stanisław
items.publisher: University of Warsaw, Formal Linguistics Department digital library
items.note: Sets out the assumptions of the Polish conversational system MARYSIA, described as inspired by the ELIZA-type programs of MIT with their interchangeable scripts.

items.title: Reanimating ELIZA, the world's first chatbot
items.author: Garfinkel, Simson L.
items.note: Review of Inventing ELIZA describing the team's reconstruction and historical placement of the program, its transcripts and later chatbots.

items.title: Weizenbaum. Rebel at Work
items.author: Haas, Peter; Holzinger, Silvia
items.note: 80-minute documentary, in English and German, on Weizenbaum's career and personal life, covering the ELIZA/DOCTOR program, 1950s computer development and SLIP; the filmmakers date it 2006 and the Computer History Museum catalogue 2007.

items.title: Plug & Pray
items.author: Schanze, Jens
items.publisher: Mascha Film; distributed by United Docs
items.note: German documentary on AI and robotics, 91 minutes, premiered at Visions du Reel on 18 April 2010, with ELIZA's creator Weizenbaum as a main protagonist set against Kurzweil, Ishiguro and other researchers; he died during production.

items.title: WEIZENBAUM J., Puissance de l'ordinateur et raison de l'homme
items.author: Pomian-Saatdjian, Joanna
items.note: Short French review of the translation of Computer Power and Human Reason in an issue on the origins of artificial intelligence; metadata only read.

items.title: [Review of "Computer Power and Human Reason" by Joseph Weizenbaum]
items.author: Lederberg, Joshua
items.in: Stanford Artificial Intelligence Project Memo AIM-291: 6-9; Profiles in Science, US National Library of Medicine
items.note: Lederberg's review of the book, held separately in his papers.

items.title: ELIZA scriptwriter's manual: a manual for the use of the ELIZA conversational computer system
items.author: Hayward, Paul R.
items.note: Manual for writing scripts for the extended ELIZA system used for tutorials at MIT.

items.title: World's first chatbot 'Eliza' revived from 60-year-old computer code
items.author: Shaikh, Kaif
items.note: Report on the revival of the 1960s chatbot from recovered code.

items.title: Inventing ELIZA: How the First Chatbot Shaped the Future of AI
items.author: Ciston, Sarah; Berry, David M.; Hay, Anthony C.; Marino, Mark C.; Millican, Peter; Shrager, Jeff; Schwarz, Arthur I.; Weil, Peggy
items.note: Eight authors present the recovered MAD-SLIP source of ELIZA with critical code readings and historical context for the program, its transcripts and later chatbots.
items.licence: CC BY-NC-ND (per OpenAlex; version not stated there)

items.title: Computer Power and Human Reason: From Judgement to Calculation
items.author: Crowther, John F.
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: The Eliza effect and its dangers: from demystification to gender critique
items.author: Dillon, Sarah
items.note: Gives a gender critique of the Eliza effect and how it is put to work in AI research while nominally being warned against.

items.title: ELIZA, the world's first chatbot, is back online after six decades thanks to AI historians
items.author: Bastian, Matthias
items.note: Report that ELIZA runs again on its original operating system through the work of a team of historians and computer scientists.

items.title: The Limits of Computation: Joseph Weizenbaum and the ELIZA Chatbot
items.author: Berry, David M.
items.in: Weizenbaum Journal of the Digital Society 3(3)
items.note: Examines Weizenbaum's ELIZA and DOCTOR persona as the ancestor of conversational interfaces and their use in thinking about the limits of computation.
items.licence: CC BY (per OpenAlex; version not stated there)

items.title: הפסיכיאטור הדיגיטלי שלי
items.author: משמרי, אביבה
items.note: Report on the Babel reissue of Avidan's 1974 book, describing how he typed alternating lines with the ELIZA dialogue program and called the software a half-and-half partner.

items.title: Computers as "Therapists"
items.author: Weizenbaum, Joseph
items.note: Letter to Science on computers presented as therapists; metadata only read.

items.title: Interactive consulting via natural language
items.author: Shapiro, Stuart C.; Kwasny, S. C.
items.note: Gives ELIZA a script that turns it into a natural language consultant for a computer system.

items.title: Computer-Simulated Psychotherapy as an Aid in Teaching Clinical Psychology
items.author: Suler, John R.
items.note: Describes the use of Eliza as a teaching aid in undergraduate clinical psychology courses.

items.title: Natürlichsprachliche Dialogkomponente als Modell sozialer Kommunikation
items.author: Wingert, B.
items.note: German discussion of natural language dialogue components that takes Weizenbaum's non-directive language game alongside Turing's imitation game and Searle's Chinese Room.

items.title: Remembering Joe Weizenbaum, ELIZA Creator
items.author: Gardner, W. David
items.note: Obituary recalling Weizenbaum as the MIT creator of ELIZA and as a critic of claims made for artificial intelligence.

items.title: The ELIZA Effect (episode 382)
items.author: Hall, Delaney; Mars, Roman
items.note: Episode produced by Delaney Hall on Weizenbaum's ELIZA, users' emotional absorption in it, Colby's therapeutic ambitions and Weizenbaum's turn to criticism, moving to Woebot, with interviews including Pamela McCorduck, Brian Christian, Melanie Mitchell, and Naomi and Miriam Weizenbaum.

items.title: EMail from Joseph Weizenbaum to Joshua Lederberg
items.author: Weizenbaum, Joseph
items.in: Joshua Lederberg Papers, Profiles in Science, US National Library of Medicine
items.note: Electronic mail from Weizenbaum to Lederberg, filed with Lederberg's review of the book; metadata only read.

items.title: Contextual understanding by computers
items.author: Weizenbaum, Joseph
items.note: Discusses further development of ELIZA and argues for the importance of context to human and machine understanding.

items.title: ELIZA Makes a Comeback
items.author: Gee, Sue
items.note: Programming news report on the reconstruction of the original ELIZA code.

items.title: 'Inventing Eliza' Review: The Mother of All Chatbots
items.author: Hutson, Matthew
items.note: Newspaper review of Inventing ELIZA, described in the publisher's blurb as combining technical detail with cultural commentary.

items.title: The Eliza Effect Goes Global: Intelligence As Simulacrum
items.author: Weatherby, Leif
items.in: Language Machines, University of Minnesota Press
items.note: Chapter 2, pp. 79-100 of Language Machines (2025), on the Eliza effect and intelligence treated as simulacrum; Crossref's issue date of 2010 for this chapter disagrees with the book's 2025 publication.

items.title: Conversations about conversational code: on the collaborative critical code studies reading of ELIZA

items.note: Describes how an eight-person team spent about four years reading the ELIZA source recovered from the MIT archives in 2021 through collaborative critical code studies.
items.licence: CC BY (per OpenAlex; version not stated there)

items.title: Computer Power and Human Reason. From Judgment to Calculation. Joseph Weizenbaum
items.author: Hunt, Earl
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: הפסיכיאטור האלקטרוני שלי: שמונה שיחות אותנטיות עם מחשב
items.author: אבידן, דוד
items.note: Eight conversations between the poet David Avidan and the ELIZA program, published as a book in Tel Aviv in 1974 with the program credited by Avidan as an equal partner in the writing.

items.title: Joseph Weizenbaum: rejecting the technological fix
items.author: Owen, Kenneth
items.note: Profile of Weizenbaum at MIT, covering his teaching and protest against defence research; only the abstract read.

items.title: ELIZA Reanimated: The world's first chatbot restored on the world's first time sharing system
items.author: Lane, Rupert; Hay, Anthony; Schwarz, Arthur; Berry, David M.; Shrager, Jeff
items.note: Reports the discovery of an ELIZA printout in Weizenbaum's MIT archives and the rebuilding of the program to run on restored CTSS on an emulated IBM 7094.

items.title: 'ELIZA,' the world's 1st chatbot, was just resurrected from 60-year-old computer code
items.author: Killgrove, Kristina
items.note: Report on the recovery of the code from Weizenbaum's papers and its revival on an emulated IBM 7094.

items.title: PARRY Encounters the DOCTOR
items.author: Cerf, Vinton G.
items.note: Transcript of a September 1972 ARPANET session in which Colby's PARRY at SAIL conversed with a DOCTOR running at BBN Tenex, reached from UCLA.

items.title: Computer Power and Human Reason: From Judgment to Calculation
items.author: Agassi, Joseph
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: הבינה של אבידן ואלייזה המלאכותית
items.author: מור, גל
items.note: Interview with Zvi Yanai, then head of public relations at IBM Israel, who says an early ELIZA came from IBM in the US on punched cards for Avidan's roughly 15 hours of terminal sessions and doubts the book's claim of minimal editing.

items.title: Edmund Berkeley and Joseph Weizenbaum
items.author: Roach, Rebecca
items.note: Guest post on the ELIZA Archaeology project website on Edmund Berkeley and Joseph Weizenbaum.

items.title: Clever Bots
items.author: Abumrad, Jad; Krulwich, Robert
items.note: Hour-long episode with a sustained segment in which Brian Christian and Sherry Turkle discuss ELIZA's design, the secretary story, talk of therapy booths and Weizenbaum's turn against AI, with a Weizenbaum clip from Plug & Pray.

items.title: Reading ELIZA: Critical Code Studies in Action
items.author: Berry, David M.; Marino, Mark C.
items.note: Uses critical code studies to read the recovered 1966 ELIZA source, its editable script design and its development context against the familiar account of the program.

items.title: Inventing ELIZA (Review)
items.author: Starr, Jeffrey
items.note: Blog review of Inventing ELIZA covering its history of the program, technical explanations and value to historians, with objections to repetition and print production.

items.title: Computer power and human reason
items.author: Kuipers, Benjamin; McCarthy, John; Weizenbaum, Joseph
items.note: Reaction by Kuipers and hostile review by McCarthy of Weizenbaum's book, with Weizenbaum's response to McCarthy.

items.title: If software is narrative: Joseph Weizenbaum, artificial intelligence, and the biographies of ELIZA
items.author: Natale, Simone
items.note: Uses Weizenbaum's ELIZA to propose a framework of biographies of media, following how the program's narratives shaped its meaning.

items.title: Joseph Weizenbaum, creator of Eliza, dead
items.author: Biggs, John
items.note: Short obituary identifying Weizenbaum as the creator of the Rogerian simulator Eliza.

items.title: Eliza in SNOBOL4
items.author: Duquet, Robert T.
items.note: Reimplements ELIZA in SNOBOL4, reports it as much shorter than the original program and proposes its use in a course on artificial intelligence.

items.title: WEIZENBAUM, J., "Computer Power and Human Reason"
items.author: Reeves, Alan
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: ELIZA: A Computer Program For the Study of Natural Language Communication Between Man and Machine
items.author: Weizenbaum, Joseph
items.note: The founding description of ELIZA, its keyword and decomposition rules, its scripts and the DOCTOR dialogue on the MAC time-sharing system at MIT.

items.title: "Hang on to the Power to Imagine": An Interview with Joseph Weizenbaum
items.author: Brady, Holly
items.note: Interview with Weizenbaum on computers in schools; metadata only read.

items.title: Social Interaction with Computers: An Interpretation of Weizenbaum¿s ELIZA and Her Heritage
items.author: Pruijt, Hans
items.note: Interprets ELIZA and its heritage as social interaction with computers, using a version of ELIZA implemented in Excel.

items.title: Weizenbaum's nightmares: how the inventor of the first chatbot turned against AI
items.author: Tarnoff, Ben
items.note: Long read on Weizenbaum's life, ELIZA's reception and his insistence that computers must not be confused with humans.

items.title: Reactions to Weizenbaum's Book
items.author: Kuipers, Benjamin
items.in: Author's site, University of Michigan; note published in SIGART Newsletter 58
items.note: Kuipers's April 1976 reaction to Computer Power and Human Reason, posted with a 2023 reflection, naming Weizenbaum as the creator of ELIZA.

items.title: Inventing ELIZA: an exploration of the first chatbot
items.author: Marino, Mark; Ciston, Sarah; Berry, David; Hay, Anthony; Shrager, Jeff; Schwarz, Arthur; Millican, Peter
items.in: Electronic Literature Organization 2026 conference, Algorithms and Imaginaries strand
items.note: Panel on the five-year project of studying the original ELIZA source code that led to the book Inventing ELIZA.

items.title: Nervous System: The ELIZA Effect
items.author: Kalat, David
items.note: Column on the first chatbot and on natural language communication with machines.

items.title: ELIZA Reinterpreted: The world's first chatbot was not intended as a chatbot at all
items.author: Shrager, Jeff

items.author: Shah, Huma; Warwick, Kevin; Vallverdú, Jordi; Wu, Defeng

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Critics
items.author: Jones, Thomas L.

items.author: Gleick, James

items.title: E-mail from Joshua Lederberg to Joseph Weizenbaum
items.author: Lederberg, Joshua

items.title: Computer Power and Human Reason: from Judgement to Calculation
items.author: Michie, Donald
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: Computer Power and Human Reason: From Judgment to Calculation
items.author: Rising, Gerald R.
items.note: Book review of Weizenbaum's 1976 book, which recounts the ELIZA episode and its reception; record taken from metadata, text not read.

items.title: AI pioneer Joseph Weizenbaum dies
items.author: Rising, David
items.note: Wire obituary describing Weizenbaum as the inventor of the natural language program ELIZA who later grew sceptical of artificial intelligence.

items.title: ELIZA Reanimated: Restoring the Mother of All Chatbots to One of the World's First Time-Sharing Systems
items.author: Lane, Rupert; Hay, Anthony; Schwarz, Arthur; Berry, David M.; Shrager, Jeff
items.in: IEEE Annals of the History of Computing

items.note: Reports a philosophy teaching exercise in which students converse with ELIZA, the psychotherapist simulation, and use the exposure to discuss machine intelligence.

items.author: Bassett, Caroline
items.note: Explores the history and reception of ELIZA as a program approximating a Rogerian therapist, read as a history of the present for computational therapy.

items.title: Code Me a Good Reason: Joseph Weizenbaum and a Rhetoric of Ethical AI
items.author: Yang, Misti Hewatt
items.publisher: University of Maryland, College Park, Communication Theses and Dissertations
items.note: Dissertation presenting Weizenbaum as an early rhetorical theorist of computation, covering his life up to ELIZA, his disillusionment during the Vietnam War, Computer Power and Human Reason and McCarthy's response.
